Q: Revit 2026 API - document.Create.NewDetailCurve(view, spline) return null while Element is created A:

Try to use the following:

DetailCurve modernCurve = DetailCurve.Create(document, view.Id, spline.Id);

Instead of the factory method approach:

document.Create.NewDetailCurve()

Hope this helps you to solve the issue.

Q: How are cache line and next-page prefetchers made aware of page sizes? A:

I see, thank you for the info! Yes, the L1 IP stride prefetcher's effects is very evident and stable in my experiments (at least when operating within the same-page 4K boundary). What is interesting, however, is how the prefetching behavior differs when a cache line belongs, at the OS level, to a huge vs. base page. What I commonly observe when testing the train/probe accesses on base pages is that only about 1-3 lines are prefetched in advance. Whereas on huge pages, at times up to 22 lines are prefetched. The weird thing is these tested lines are all in the same 4KiB page boundary. So in theory both huge/base pages should have similar prefetching behaviors, though it seems it kicks off more aggressively for huge pages.

Q: Is there a useful case using a switch statement without braces? A:

Here's an example written by Dennis Ritchie in 1972 during his work on the first C compiler. The c02.c module, linked at the foot of page I just linked to, includes

easystmt()
{
    extern peeksym, peekc, cval;

    if((peeksym=symbol())==20)  /* name */
        return(peekc!=':');  /* not label */
    if (peeksym==19) {      /* keyword */
        switch(cval)
        case 10:    /* goto */
        case 11:    /* return */
        case 17:    /* break */
        case 18:    /* continue */
            return(1);
        return(0);
    }
    return(peeksym!=2);     /* { */
}

From reading his 1972 code it's clear Dennis was a fan of switch statements - he used them quite a bit. It's not so surprising given that almost everything was encoded as an int partly for lack of other data type possibilities. His compiler implementation used no structs at that stage because he was just in the middle of adding them to the language. Dynamic dispatch, vtables and polymorphism were a long way off. I've tried and failed to find a reference for this but if I recall correctly Dennis "invented" switch statements or at least contributed ideas leading to the form they take in C and considered them one of his best or proudest additions to the language.

The ability to leave out the braces makes switch statements formally similar to if, for, do and while statements, helping to simplify and unify the grammar. See the selection-statement and iteration-statement productions in the C grammar (e.g. in Appendix A13 of Kernighan and Ritchie, pages 236-237 in my copy) where these things are defined.

Obviously one can always add braces but maybe that seems heavy for such simple examples as this one. This example could be coded as a disjunctive if statement but I think one of the ideas Dennis had for switch was that the compiler is more clearly being offered the opportunity to optimise the implementation of the branching logic based on the particular constants involved.

Q: First participant works, second participant breaks media publishing on AWS A:

I ran into a very similar issue before, and in my case it wasn't a LiveKit Cloud problem.

The error:

PublishTrackError: publishing rejected as engine not connected within timeout

followed by:

could not createOffer with closed peer connection

usually means the WebRTC peer connection was already closed when LiveKit tried to publish or renegotiate tracks.

Looking at the code, I'd check whether the useEffect that creates the Room is being triggered more than once. The effect depends on:

[serverUrl, token, notifyLeaveComplete]

If notifyLeaveComplete changes between renders, React will run the cleanup, call room.disconnect(), and create a new room instance. That can leave LiveKit trying to publish on a connection that has already been closed.

I'd add some logging around room creation and cleanup to see if the room is being recreated when the second participant joins.

I'd also check Firefox's about:webrtc page and the browser console for ICE failures. If the signaling connection stays connected but ICE goes to failed or disconnected, then it's likely a WebRTC/network issue rather than an application issue.

Since localhost works with the same LiveKit project and tokens, my guess would be either:

  1. A React lifecycle/remount issue causing room.disconnect() unexpectedly.

  2. An ICE/WebRTC connectivity problem in production.

  3. A race condition where tracks are being published while the connection is reconnecting.

I'd start by confirming that only one Room instance exists throughout the meeting and that the effect isn't running again when participants join.

Q: How to render a property-based Svelte snippet with a pre-defined property value? A:

It is possible, but you would have to violate the internals boundary, which can break at any time. There is a long-standing issue that advocates for adding a blessed way to do this.

The hack looks like this:

let snippetToRender = $derived(
    useNoParamSnippet 
        ? noParamSnippet
        : $anchor => stringParamSnippet(
            $anchor,
            () => textToUseInStringParamSnippet,
          )
);

Playground

The first argument of the function generated by #snippet is the insertion point node.
And arguments have to be passed as functions, so they can retain reactivity.

(The server-side rendering signature is different.)

Q: Failure to create a new Firebase project: Failure to add Firebase to Google Cloud Platform project. 403 PERMISSION_DENIED A:

I'm not sure what is causing the 403 error, but the simplest way to fix it is probably to go to the Firebase console and connect the existing Google Cloud Project to Firebase there.

According to the documentation on How to add Firebase to an existing Google Cloud project, that nowadays works by:

  1. Go to the Firebase console
  2. Click Create new Firebase project
  3. Click Add Firebase to Google Cloud project at the bottom left
  4. Select your project in the Select a Google Cloud project field

After this you can re-run the flutterfire CLI, and select the Firebase project (rather than creating a new one).
